Recipe:
Stuff(Me)ing 8-10 Servings Based on a Recipe from Karla Therriault
§ion;
Most Thanksgivings we have used boxes of Stove Top Stuffing, but one year we ate at our in-laws, the Therriault's, and fell in love with their stuffing. Karla gave us her recipe and we made some modifications to make it completely on the stove instead of stuffing it into the Turkey. That makes it Stuff(Me)ing instead of Stuffing. &smiley;
Cut Onion into ¼-inch discs, then slice the discs into 8 wedges.
Cut Celery into thin slices. Slice the leaves into the same thickness.
Chop Sage Leaves until pieces are ⅛-inch squares or smaller. Remove Thyme Leaves from stems, but don't chop.
If Mushrooms are not already sliced, cut into ¼&inch; thick slices. (If slices are more than 1½&inch; wide, cut in half from top to bottom.)
Using a Bread knife, cut Bread slices into 1-inch x 1-inch squares. (This can be done with several slices at a time.)
Then place Bread cubes into a large bowl.
In a saucepan, melt the Butter then stir in the Onion, Celery, Sage, Thyme, Salt and Pepper.
Reduce heat to low, and simmer with lid on, stirring occasionally, for 20 minutes.
Add Mushrooms and simmer for 5 minutes. Add Turkey Broth, turn burner to high and bring to a boil. Pour Turkey Broth mixture over the Bread cubes and gently stir until all of the Bread has absorbed some Broth. Let sit for 5 minutes and gently stir again.
If a Thanksgiving Turkey is being prepared:
Take the Giblets (neck, gizzard, liver, and heart) from inside the Turkey.
Put them in a small pot with an amount of Water matching the amount of Turkey Broth needed, plus ½ Cup.
Bring to a boil, then turn to low and let simmer for 1-2 hours.
Filter out the Giblets and use the remaining liquid as the Turkey Broth.
Alternatively, the Turkey Broth can be obtained from the Turkey's drippings when it is done cooking.
Instead of using fresh Bread, use dried Bread cubes or pieces. (Di's favorite is from Haggens!)
Then increase the Turkey Broth to 1 Cup per 8 Oz. bag or package of dried Bread.
If not being prepared as a side dish for turkey, use chicken, vegetable, or some other flavor of broth.
Instead of Fresh Sage and Thyme, dried can be used. If you gently crush them before adding, it helps release more flavor.
Add 2-4 Oz. fully cooked Sausage, broken into pea-sized chunks, just before adding the bread.
